system.name: Vega
system.description: The fifth brightest star in the sky and a cornerstone of astronomical photometry. Vega is an A0 star 25 light-years away, nearly pole-on as seen from Earth, surrounded by a dusty debris disk suggesting planet formation.

vega.name: Vega
vega.description: An A0Va blue-white star spinning so rapidly — once every 12.5 hours — that its equator bulges outward, making it visibly oblate. It is surrounded by a large debris disk seen nearly face-on from Earth, which may hint at an unseen planetary system.
vega.funFact: Vega served as the photometric calibration standard for over a century — when astronomers assign a star magnitude 0, they mean it looks as bright as Vega. It will also become Earth's pole star around the year 13,700 CE.
